candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: The mechanic of having to fire a ball to choose which path you take completely ruins the entire game for me. Being able to choose your path in a roguelike like this is so insanely important, it can effectively tank your entire run just because your ball randomly bounces into the wrong path option.Most of the time you have clean shots to go where you want, and only risk ending up on the wrong path if you get get greedy and try to grab some extra coins on the way. This is fine, as a risk-reward mechanic. The problem is when you have paths that randomly spawn impossible mazes of pegs before you choose, making where you end up almost completely random. This happens, at least once, literally every run. Imagine if, in StS, you moved to click on an elite to get a sweet artifact, and the game sometimes says 'no' and moved you to a random, much worse spot on the board, that then locks you into a chain of bad options that you didn't want. It's a pretty awful, no-win, feel-bad mechanic. This is extra bad because, in Peglin, some paths are just obviously, objectively worse than others. In StS and most games, no matter which path you take you get the same number of nodes. Some are better than others, but you always get a chance for an equal *number* of rewards, if not reward quality.In this game, some paths just have significantly fewer reward nodes (in addition to being worse); they will just skip over free chests altogether, not replacing them with anything else. And sometimes this is completely out of your control. In a game that is already 100x more random than most skill-based roguelikes, the fact that you can't even guarantee agency in what path you take kills the whole experience for me. Solid thumbs down.

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: Sometimes the layout of the pegs makes lengthy chain reactions less likely, or maybe the special pegs are located in hard to hit places.My complaint isn’t about the game being too hard. I won my third run and I’ve beaten the second level of cruciball (there are 20 difficulty levels which add extra modifiers, similar to other deckbuilders). But this extra layer of randomness (on top of the usual roguelite randomness relating to which items you’ll be offered in each shop, what order the orbs will be drawn in each fight, which bosses you need to fight during this run, etc) removes any possibility of playing tactically. I can’t plan ahead to the next turn because I’ve got no idea which pegs will be hit (or restored) with the current shot. And when I lose, I don’t feel like I can learn and improve, I just feel like “the bounce screwed me, there was nothing else I could do”.Each run uses a familiar node structure including normal and elite fights, random events, and relic chests. But when selecting the next node to travel to, you have to shoot an orb through the relevant gap at the bottom of the screen, so there’s a chance the orb will bounce off a peg and go in the opposite direction. Oh, you wanted to go to the chest to get a relic? Well actually, why don’t you fight some more enemies instead.Maybe if Peglin had released a couple of years ago when I first added it to my wishlist, I might feel better about it. But this is the problem with early access games. The longer it takes to finish development, the more likely you get overshadowed by newer games. Peglin doesn’t compare favourably to other recent releases in the roguelite genre such as Balatro and Cobalt Core.I received a copy of this game as a gift from work colleagues.

question: What makes Kingdom Rush Vengeance stand out compared to other tower defense games?

candidates.title: Kingdom Rush Vengeance - Tower Defense review
candidates.text: The Kingdom Rush games have always been one of the best and most entertaining tower defense games I have ever played. Kingdom Rush Vengeance is the 4th installment in the series. Although you are fighting for the evil side this time, Ironhide Studio has still added plenty of hidden references, easter eggs, comedy, and strategy that go so well with their games. You also have a fair number of interesting heroes to take control and aid you on the battlefield.Vengeance is probably the most difficult of the four. What makes it more difficult than previous games is the vast number of towers to use. In previous games you have 4 towers that can branch into two different towers giving you a total of 8 different towers. Now, Vengeance got rid of the branching towers and instead gave you 18 different towers to unlock and use. You can only bring 5 towers to each level so picking which towers to use is very important.Heroes are still a very powerful force to aid you wherever you need their help, but in Vengeance it is even more important to bring the right hero. Heroes will either deal physical or magical damage, so make sure you have the right one to exploit the enemies weakness.If you are new to the series or even to tower defense games, I would recommend starting with the first Kingdom Rush before jumping into this one. The game is still enjoyable and a must have for anyone that is a fan to the games.

candidates.title: Kingdom Rush Vengeance - Tower Defense review
candidates.text: This is absolutely the worst KR. The dynamics they had in the other games are gone. In earlyer KR each tower could be uppgrade. In this game only the hero and magic skills was possible to uppgrade. I get bored realy fast of this game compared to the other.

candidates.title: Kingdom Rush Vengeance - Tower Defense review
candidates.text: Perhaps Kingdom Rush Vengeance is good when considered in a vacuum, but since I don't live in a vacuum I can't recommend it. The Kingdom Rush tower defense games are generally excellent, but in my opinion this is the worst of the bunch. Since the other games are nearly identical, I recommend playing an earlier Kingdom Rush game instead.The main difference with Kingdom Rush Vengeance is that stars you earn don't mean anything. In earlier Kingdom Rush games, the better you do, the more stars you earn, and beating the optional challenge modes gives even more stars, and stars are what you used to unlock upgrades. In Kingdom Rush Vengeance, you get the same number of upgrade points no matter how well you do, and beating the optional challenge modes does not give any additional upgrade points. That takes away most of the reason to try to get a top score or to beat the extra challenge modes.My second complaint - and people may disagree here - is with the unlockable towers. In general, I like tower defense games whose difficulty doesn't depend on how much grinding you've done or how far you've gotten in an upgrade tree. That's why my favorite Kingdom Rush tower defense game is probably the first, where even heroes did not have persistent upgrades. This forces the developers to design better levels. The more the difficulty depends on unlockables and choosing the right heroes and towers and having the right hero upgrades, the less it depends on pure strategy relating to the level design itself. That said, if you like upgrade trees and having lots of different ways to beat a level, you'll probably like the unlockable towers. One benefit of the unlockable towers is that they make the puzzle levels that restrict you to two tower types more interesting.Overall I just can't recommend Kingdom Rush Vengeance - not because it's bad, but just because the other Kingdom Rush games are better and cheaper.

candidates.title: Baldur's Gate 3 review
candidates.text: I want to preface this review with a quick reminder that this is my personal view. Not everyone will have the same view of something. But, keeping in mind that this was my experience, the review could be useful to some.As a DnD in a digital form, this game did manage to get many of the mechanics in. That being said, large parts of dnd rules are full of holes and issues that have to be fixed at the table between GM and players. And a huge amount of the fun that can be had at a dnd table is due to the people at the table, not the rules on it. So, anyone with a lot of experience playing dnd with a group might find it hard to enjoy their rules put in a strict virtual rule set. Looking past that, the mechanics of the game seemed well implemented. This is still a do-not-recommend, though.Loved the idea of this game, but, I'm impossibly bored by the race lineup. Human, halfling, gnome, and dwarf are all pretty good. The dragonborn seemed like a cool race to look forward too, but they just look so off too me. That's personal taste, of course. And, then the rest of the race list is build-a-elf. Be it dark elf, high elf, wood elf, half-elf, or star trek alien elf. Just. Eh.Other than that, I did have some issues with the overall storytelling. Of the grab bag of fantastic and colorful characters you can bump into, none of them were relatable. Sort of gave off vibes of trying to RP with a player that cared too much about their cool backstory to remember that their character can have conversations like a normal person too.And the main story has the party assemble because of a massive mind flayer ship and all the main characters getting larvae put in their brains (not a spoiler, that's the beginning). First problem is that it's almost TOO fantastic of a start.

candidates.title: GWENT: The Witcher Card Game review
candidates.text: TOO MANY NEGATIVE ASPECTS THAT ULTIMATELY DAMAGE USER EXPERIENCE OF A GAME WHICH HAD MUCH POTENTIAL TO BE GREAT ;(The game has been designed to be a far more complex and challenging variant of Gwent than players are used to in The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt. But that does not take the fun and immersiveness out of the game. What does however constantly annoy and ultimately discourage a player from investing much time into the game are some persistent issues that make the game at sometimes a horrible experience. Looking into the details online, as long as your production is high, you're fine. You can ignore literally everything else. There is a ton of potential here for this game if the warfare settings were revised or even able to be changed, and balancing was implemented to ensure that the various aspects of society are better reflected, such as research, production, culture growth, faith, food production etc. Overall, I can not recommend the game in its current state, even on sale. There is a lot of potential here, and plenty of hype from game review sites, however I encourage anyone whos interested in the game to read up on the mechanics before buying it. Look into the balance issues, AI issues, and warfare mechanics before pulling the trigger on this game so you wont be disappointing like I was.

You lose 1% total score for each colony in this state, per turn.The singular game breaking problem is that it is entirely possible that a planet might actually have no possible way to meet its basic needs. It is entirely possible (in my experience, about 50% chance) there are no networks within the visible starting planets that can be self sustaining. This means you'll have to just build anyway and _hope_ that something you can't see will be exactly what you need.If it ISN'T what you need, and it rarely is, then you've lost the game. There's no game mechanics that allow you to change a planet to another colony type or bulldoze the colony altogether to prevent permanently 1% happiness per turn. There are game mechanics to increase happiness, but they're balanced such that you could easily spend dozens of research points deep in the tech tree to just get 1% of what you've lost back. There's an undo feature, but it is disabled every time you as the player execute any action that gives you information, so this does nothing to mitigate this problem either. It's obviously frustrating when this happens immediately at the start of a run, but it's even more frustrating half way through successful run.All of this means you'll be restarting a lot. candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: The game is trying to be a horror game and a roguelike RPG, but completely fails in both regards. In reality, World of Horror is a management simulation game where you are constantly trying to manage your ever dwindling health counter, sanity counter, and the ticking clock "doom meter". Ultimately, you will soon realize that the best strategy is to rush through the game as fast as you can to keep the doom meter low and hope RNG blesses you with enough health and sanity to get through the last stage's boss rush. Sadly, this strategy is no fun, but neither is having your run cut short constantly by the doom meter.Beyond that, the mystery's don't feel connected to the overarching threat of the "old god" you picked as your antagonist, nor do they even feel connected to each other. Whether you pick the Ancient Egyptian Fire God or the Lovecraftian Spider God, you are going to be playing the same 5 mysteries that seem completely unconnected to them.It is a shame, because the artwork is great, the music is great, and I can see the framework of a potentially great game in place, but it feels like it was doomed long ago from flawed gameplay mechanics and ideas that they refused to scrap or reinvent.

candidates.title: Borderlands 3 review
candidates.text: Borderlands had a lot to live up to with 2, impossibly high standards I'd say. As such, 3 did a lot better than what we give it credit for, I think. The story is lack luster in some areas and some of the npcs/dialogue are awkward but there's plenty of dialogue and missions that are funny and in classic BL fashion. I think most of the recurring characters were paid a decent homage (though others were did downright dirty). Zane has my favorite PC dialogue by far. The only missions I downright hated were the ones with required vehicles, because once your car blew up you had to WALK to respawn a new one and it ruined the flow of the game. BL3 by far excelled in mechanics and guns. The game play is quicker, smoother, and keeps you on your toes even with maxed out stats and guns. The extra mobility mechanics makes it much more fun to get up in the enemy's grill and light em up, and now parkour is easier than ever. I've beat the campaign like three times and I still had a blast each time, I can't wait to try some of the DLCs. The guns (and equipment in general) are much more diversified and the manufacturers are much more unique. 2K really had fun with some of the abilities. Overall, Borderlands came a long way from the first game and while some titles excelled in some ways and failed in others, I feel that each title still got progressively better. BL3 is no exception.

candidates.title: Teardown review
candidates.text: Teardown is absolutely beautiful. Every level is a voxel landscape that puts the environmental design of dozens of other games to shame. Offices, manors, docks, what have you, every level is packed with immense character and atmosphere, there are no prefab buildings put in to just take up space. Every single room is packed with goodies to smash, which is the point of all this voxel stuff. Everything breaks and Teardown is nothing but an engine to make beautiful things for you to run through and break. Taking a blowtorch to a locked door latch and watching the door swing freely open as a matter of physics, or cutting a hole in a chain link fence and grabbing the cut part of the fence and tossing it aside is an unmatched tactile joy in gaming. That's just leaving off the chaos you can wreak on entire rooms or BUILDINGS. You can even place planks if you want to do the opposite and actually build things.The problem is the game attached to it all is just plain boring. I don't know if you CAN make a good game this focused on physics but Teardown did not succeed. You get SOME variety but most of the levels are time trials. Go into the empty environment, plot a route through all the objectives. Break routes, prepare vehicles, and when you're ready to start, grab one of the objectives, starting a timer forcing you to grab all of them and then leg it before game over. The prep work for this is horrible. You walk in person all over the map with no fast travel having to plot these routes meticulously. Vehicles are vital but they are voxel modeled as well so if you brush them into anything they disintegrate into uselessness instantly. Boats do not run aground they just dissolve. Take a ramp too hard or a bush the wrong way and you're now driving half a car.

candidates.title: Teardown review
candidates.text: The campaign isn't bad, but it isn't what alot of players was expecting, and many do not find it fun. Challenge mode is mostly for your own amusement, or to compare scores with friends allowing you to steal items in a certain amount of time or destroy as much of the stage you can in 60 seconds (in which the timer starts after the destruction of 1000 voxels, giving you some leeway to plan your destruction). Sandbox allows you to roam the levels with few restrictions - your "weapons" have unlimited uses, and you don't have to worry about alarms. You still have a health bar, but you can respawn shortly after death with no penalty. grappling hooks, jetpacks, lightsabers, black holes, Rocket Launchers, Guns, Portal Guns, Physics Guns Tanks, AC-130s, Nuclear Bombs, the HE Blade from Metal Gear Rising Revengence to sling waves of energy through the entire map or an Omnicutter that does about the same thing, but you can paint a shape of what it cuts or fall back to a Railgun that shoots a simple, big hole through whatever it passes and loads more. Teardown's "Modability" allows the potential for infinite ways to create and destroy voxels. However, there is no end goal to this, and this only serves to play around with destruction, which can lose its appeal very quickly. You've destroyed the voxel replica of an airplane, Titanic ship, or big city? Now what? Do it again with other tools I suppose. This does mean the fun of Teardown is limited to your own imagination and ability to find the fun of breaking things for "breaking things sake" and no other reward, outside of recording it for video or live streaming.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: 这是我见过内核最恶心最可怕的游戏。 仅从游戏来看，画面风格很好，音乐不错，以及在视觉上omori这个保护人格所创造梦境世界确实挺有童话感。 但是游戏的玩法设计却毁了这些；首先无聊的战斗，战斗给我的感觉完全可以完全舍弃，感情克制在大多数世界里完全用不到干莽就完了，在与一些boss战斗时boss会强制修改自己的情感或投放技能混乱玩家的情感buff，所以在boss战斗的中后期也基本上是莽，情感克制只能前面多打些伤害。 解密更是糟糕，真的是没有一个可以让人感到会心一笑的，全部都是那种一眼便知还要玩命绕路拖时间的。 支线也是跑路拿东西和杀怪居多，没有凸显出不同地图的特点。 最糟心的是梦境世界和现实的目的几乎完全割裂，玩家是可以从冒险中看到一些Sunny自身黑暗面的线索，但对Sunny面对自己的罪行却没有一点帮助，无论你杀了多少boss收集了多少物品做了多少支线也都只是在Omori人格创造的虚假乐园里冒险而已，我全程看不到Sunny本人格的一点挣扎，所以我觉得如果只是单纯在表现Omori的虚假世界的美好与现实情况进行对比的话，完全可以舍去全部的梦境战斗这样只留最后和Omori的战斗会更有仪式感，并缩短梦境世界的流程，比如超级甜心的剧情明显过长而且对主线毫无帮助；更专注与设计解密，小游戏配合少量支线这样会舒服。 在现实世界线设计师把前期开门关门作为分支给个人感觉还可以，问题是之后玩家很多选择但其实流程却本质就是一个纯线性的流程，甚至一场战斗你打赢打输之后npc的台词都是差不多的也没任何奖励，而支线，收集又是一样对主线塑造乃至人物塑造都毫无帮助，这让为了想看新东西反复试错的我很不能接受。

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: Omori's pastel-hued world holds a surprising amount of darkness, beautifully captured in its hand-drawn artwork. Lushly detailed environments shift seamlessly into dreamlike landscapes, while character designs range from adorable plushies to grotesquely fascinating creatures. The story masterfully builds uncanny tension, not through cheap jump scares, but by immersing you in a world steeped in unsettling secrets and veiled anxieties.However, Omori's biggest hurdle lies in its pacing. candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: I decided to pick up Omori because of it's unique and charming art direction. After completing it, I can tell you that this title has loads more to offer than just its visual flair. The story depicted in Omori is quite gripping with a healthy dose of humour added in just the right places. However when the narrative requires it, the funny quips and one-liners are cast aside in favour of powerful writing that will most definitely tug at your heart strings. Omori was capable of making me laugh, bringing me to a verge of tears and make me tremble in fear. Moreover to give credit where credit is due the gameplay is very fun and creative. One criticism that could be levied at Omori's combat system is the amount of random encounters which at times got a bit tedious to say the least. This issue is especially prevalent when backtracking through a location. However it is important to mention that this did not make me dislike Omori's gameplay, quite the contrary. Even if repetitive at times, the combat and exploration were very fun and rewarding. The bossfights were also a highlight of my experience with the game. Every boss we face in Omori is beautifully designed and full of personality.As i have mentioned the art style is also a major apeal of the game. Every character is unique not only in how they are written but also how the look. In other words the visuals perfectly complement the narrative. The same applies to a certain degree to the enemies we face during our journey through the Headspace. Although some more variety in this case would be a welcome change it isn't a major criticism on my behalf. Especially taking into account that this is addressed by the creatively nightmarish creations we sometimes get to face. I will gladly accept quality over quantity and let me tell you that quality is most definitely what we get. To summarise Omori is overall an amazing, fun and emotionally engaging experience. I wholeheartedly recommend it.

candidates.text: I’ve played many physics games & tend to like them. And Besiege had some good points. It was relaxing, had decent graphics & well-developed strategy.But overall, I did not like Besiege & do NOT recommend it. In short, I was underwhelmed & not impressed.First, I hated that the game lacks a tutorial. The game was in early access for 5 years & the developers failed to include this basic feature. Seriously? The game Teardown is in early access, & I bought it only a few months after it was first released. And Teardown came with a helpful tutorial.Moreover, I found the gameplay to be somewhat laborious, & anticlimactic. It felt like you needed an encyclopedia just to learn how to build anything very interesting. And then after so much effort, the result is a quick, uninteresting destruction or your fragile vehicle quickly gets broken. I don’t want to rack my brain for such unsatisfying results. Plus, the torch weapon and the vehicles I created never made a sound. Fire makes a sound in real life. Burning makes a sound in real life. Hearing nothing in the game was disappointing & anticlimactic.Also, I found the physics to be boring, somewhat unrealistic, & repetitive. Items all were destroyed in the same way, regardless of what weapon was used. The soldiers’ physics were likewise a turn off. Their movement consisted of them bouncing around like little Lego men & they took no damage when you ran them over with your created vehicle. And the soldiers all died the same way, regardless of how you killed them. It was disappointing & uninteresting. The destruction animations were seriously flawed.If you’re the engineering type or you want to do lots of research to build medieval vehicles & you love puzzles/strategy/campaigns, then you might like Besiege.

question: What is the main goal of the 'Hellblade EX: Hunt' quest?

candidates.title: Fist of Guthix/Strategies
candidates.text:
The hunter's objective is quite simple: Kill the hunted player with any means necessary. The player cannot gather any charges while they are a hunter, rather their objective is to prevent the hunted player from gathering charges. The hunter does not have a stat decrease, does not have the 30 kg load of the stone and does not take damage from the energy charges, however they cannot chase hunted players into the teleport houses.

In general, people who start as the hunter have the advantage. This can be due to being able to get a general idea of how many charges your opponent has and being able to do what you want without fear of your opponent retaliating.

Use a Familiar to help you hunt. Considering the fact that most players do not think to use Protect from Summoning,this can be devastating to your target.

Effective weapons, spells and effects include Ancient Magicks Ice Spells, which hold an opponent and can be devastating to an opponent's health. Inflicting the opponent with poison is good if a player is along the outside or house hugging, since anti-poison potion is not allowed. When using range, using a crossbow with Sapphire bolts (e) in conjunction with Smite is very effective as this will reduce the hunted's Prayer level very quickly.

It is advised to have melee gear along with magic or ranged gear, whatever the players level is higher.

The special attack of the Ancient mace which is obtained after completing Another Slice of H.A.M. lowers a players prayer by amount of damage done and gives it to you, which will help drain the hunted's prayer. Combined with smite or Soul Split, you could possibly remove more than 400 prayer points from your opponent in one strike!

Using 2h swords is useful, as you can deal a lot of damage when you get the chance and it will be likely that your hunted is running.

candidates.text: Greek Gods: Featured prominently in God of War, God of War II, God of War: Betrayal, God of War: Chains of Olympus, God of War III, God of War: Ghost of Sparta, and God of War: Ascension. A great part of the Pantheon was wiped out by Kratos. Initially led by Cronos ruling over the Titan Gods from Mount Orthys, until being overthrown by his son Zeus who ruled over the Olympian Gods from Mount Olympus. Norse Gods: Featured prominently in God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarök. Split between the warlike Aesir led by the knowledge-hungry Odin and the nature-loving Vanir led by the witch-like Freya. Egyptian Gods: Mentioned in God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarök, and featured in God of War: Fallen God. They are half-human, half-animal Gods who, from what Mimir heard, rule with wisdom and humility.God of War Ragnarök, Goal: Stolen Treasures, Ankh (Codex Entry) According to Mimir, they are many and not as simple to qualify as "good" or "evil".God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: The Black Rune They are featured on a tapestry showing Týr's journeys and the Egyptian symbol of the Eye_of_Ra Eye of Ra is on Týr's missing triptych panel.God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: A Path to Jötunheim Only the Gods ThothGod of War: Fallen God and SekhmetGod of War Laufey have appeared so far. Egyptian hieroglyphs are also one of the three languages engraved on the Mask of Creation. Mayan Gods: Alluded to in God of War (2018) and mentioned in God of War Ragnarök.

candidates.title: Cinéma Vérité
candidates.text:
A fed-ex quest that takes you back to the luxurious Monster Army bunker. The cinema theater is the goal here, defended by four laser grids. To recap, the levers are: In the dead-end corridor leading west from the lobby, in the "basement" area with the bomb hoppers, in the control room, and in the storage chamber west of the control room. The theater has not one, not two, but THREE robots that require defeating: A Shockdog and two Drilldogs. After defeating them, loot the area, especially the movie reels by the stage.
Return to Eid. The reels are severely damaged, so she'll ask you to participate in crafting a proper narrative out of them (you get to choose the heroes, the setting, and then the title; if you have companions, you can volunteer them to help. Darius Kwon loves the opportunity as does Fishlips. The quest completes after that.

candidates.title: Afterlife
candidates.text:
In order to save his ill son Atreus, Kratos journeyed into Helheim to retrieve the heart of the Keeper of the Bridge of the Damned with his Blades of Chaos. After killing Máttugr Helson and retrieving his heart, the mists of Helheim haunt Kratos with a vision of his father. Mimir assures him that it's not real. The information from this though is what leads Mimir to realize that Kratos was the Ghost of Sparta.God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: The Sickness

Later, Kratos, Atreus, Mimir and Baldur are thrown into Helheim, beyond the Bridge of the Damned, by the sudden use of the Bifröst in Týr's Temple. Atreus is tormented by a vision of him killing Modi, but Kratos reassures him. The trio then find Baldur, and secretly watch the vision that haunts him. There, they learn that Freya is Baldur's mother, and that she took away his ability to feel in order to protect him. The group makes its way into a ship docked in Helheim Landing, and modify it to make it fly up the waterfall. During the travel, Kratos is once again tormented by a vision of Zeus, this time of Kratos killing him with his bare fists. All the while, Hraesvelg flaps his wings, and the ship reaches Týr's Temple.God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: Escape from Helheim

candidates.title: Team Update - June 2025
candidates.text:
Throughout the summer we plan to implement a variety of upcoming QoL changes; everything from removing Tripod Levels & Epic Engravings to improving the support experience.

Two QoL systems we haven’t discussed previously are the Battle Analyzer feature (a feature that displays the player’s battle performance to themselves) and the Comprehensive Battle Score (a form of Gear Score that factors in a variety of power vectors). For these systems, we’re excited to implement as we believe that they will help players better understand their contributions on the battlefield, but will be on the lookout for toxicity created by these systems. We hope that other changes will help mitigate gatekeeping and toxicity, such as the updates to Mokoko Bootcamp, raid difficulty decreases, and the Kazeros Raid resurrection system.

We're still evaluating the Bound Gem changes for the Western release, and are aiming to have a further update in the next Roadmap.

Mileage Shop

Our policy for the Mileage Shop will be providing 10% of Royal Crystals spent through the in-game shop as “Prestige Points”, which can be exchanged for a variety of rewards in the Mileage Shop. It’s important to note that Prestige Points are not awarded for Steam DLC or MTX items, or for items purchased with Crystals. This will also retroactively apply to past Royal Crystal expenditures. We are currently targeting August for the full release of the Mileage Shop.

API

Our team hit some delays in releasing the feature from when we initially stated we were looking into releasing it in the West, but we are still actively investigating the path forward. We know it can be frustrating for those who were eagerly anticipating its arrival, but didn’t want to remain silent on the topic when we know it’s important to various players, content creators, and fan sites. We will continue to work on this behind the scenes, and will provide a more concrete update when we’re able to.

question: What does Voghiln say about his fighting style?

candidates.title: Sindri
candidates.text:
Sindri was later encountered in the ruins of the village after Kratos and Atreus brought the giant hammer down upon the ice, remarking that he thought it was best he moved his shop before Thor's "idiot" sons showed up. After being questioned by Kratos about Magni and Modi, Sindri began to describe their family history, before being cut off by the impatient Spartan who demanded to know about their weaponry and fighting style. The dwarf told him that Magni was incredibly strong and carried a huge sword that was hardened by cyclonic thunder, but described Modi's weaponry as a cheap knock-off of his fathers hammer and remarked he would sooner lick a rat than shake his hand.

After Atreus is cured of his sickness and learns that he is a God, they encounter Sindri again at the Foothills. As Sindri once again starts to talk negatively about his brother, Atreus becomes annoyed, telling the dwarf to either do something about it or shut up, remarking that he and his father are sick of hearing about "little people's little problems", which noticeably upsets Sindri. Kratos later reprimands Atreus for his unkind words, reminding Atreus that his mother would not have agreed with his approach. Sindri is noticeably sarcastic to the pair whenever they approach one of his shops from that point onwards.

candidates.title: The Bridge to Nowhere
candidates.text:
The mission's dialogue varies depending on the player's Honor level:
If the player has high Honor, Arthur says how leaving the gang would allow John to "give something to Jack." If the player has low Honor, Arthur tells John: "There's no reason for you to be sticking around at this point."
When John asks Arthur about loyalty, Arthur replies: "Be loyal to what matters," if he has high Honor, but with: "That’s long been broken," if his Honor is low. When John asks Arthur what he will do, high Honor Arthur will not be forthcoming and say: "I'll be okay. But do it, for me. And it would make me... feel... good, if that makes any sense." If Arthur's Honor is low, he says that he will stay in the gang and talk about the "'code' that they had". If Arthur's Honor is high, he says that they are fighting for "An idea that don't work no more," whereas low Honor Arthur says that they are fighting for "A silly idea. It don't even exist."
After saying that he is "seeing things lot more clearly now," and that he "wishes things were different..." high Honor Arthur says: "But it weren't us who changed," while low Honor Arthur says: "...but I ain't being taken for a fool no more!"
There are two bits of foreshadowing quotes in this mission that Arthur will remember during his final ride to camp in the "Red Dead Redemption" mission if his Honor is high:
At the beginning, John questions Dutch's loyalty, saying, "I feel like I just don't know Dutch anymore."
When John asks Arthur about loyalty, Arthur replies, "You know, all that ever mattered to me was loyalty. It was all I knew.

candidates.title: Library Of Ruina review
candidates.text: In addition, using many cards per turn -- which is necessary to keep up with the enemy force's onslaught -- costs a lot of Light resource to do, and inevitably your characters will also 'crap out' due to a lack of Light mana to actually cast their cards.As consequence, EVERY DECK is required to have cards that draw more cards, as well as cards that add Light back into your pool. A deck that does not have both will 'crap out' and become useless after ~4-6 turns.This doesn't sound bad until I tell you that a deck can have different 9 cards, with a limit of 3 copies per card.Ergo, a third -- or more -- of your deck is SOLELY populated by light-card recovery cards, and this is an efficient build. Late-game, many of these recovery cards require the pseudo-buff called Charge to use, where Charge is generated using certain cards and is expended using the recovery cards.This means that, in the late-game, your deck will consist of:- 2 - 3 cards to generate Charge.- 2 - 3 cards to expend Charge, recover Light, and draw cards.- 3 - 5 cards to actually play the game with.With, at MINIMUM, half of your deck being dedicated SOLELY to recovering light and drawing cards... you can see where the creativity in builds die, right?In addition, each character can use a set of passive abilities called a 'Keypage', where equipping a different Keypage grants that character with different health stats, speed values, resistances, and passive abilities. Many of these Keypages in the late-game necessitate that they are built a specific way, or are damned to be useless. Many of them end up falling off entirely, and become unusable.EDIT, MANY HOURS LATER:I still agree with a majority of the points here, having beaten the game and played it over again, many times.

candidates.title: General
candidates.text: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic is a video game in the genre of city builders. The game is a real-time city builder game, a player's choice immediately affects the game, the game reacts to it. The game is Soviet-themed meaning that the objects a player places in the game world has the characteristics of real Soviet objects. You can think of the architecture of buildings, vehicles, how power lines and heat-pipes look like in the real world. The game is also a kind of tycoon game, the player is in charge of companies and industries to build the ultimate self-sufficient republic.

If 'Auto search' is enabled the Construction office will look for enabled construction types. These construction types can be enabled or disabled from the Construction office. Construction types are:

When 'Auto search' is disabled the player has complete control over which construction site to start constructing. The player has to take care of assigning each and every individual construction site, to the construction office, that has to be built.

Every construction site that has been assigned to the construction office, manually or automatically, will be added to a list in that construction office. candidates.text: Story: I love XCOM series and I found myself wanting to skip all lines and all story of this game. Nothing makes sense.XCOM used to be great because all details seemed really thought out and that it was actually something that could happen in real life. candidates.title: Helios
candidates.text:
FEEL THE POWER OF THE SUN! Helios attacking Kratos
As the God of the Sun and easily one of the most important deities in the Greek Pantheon, Helios is implied to be an incredible force to be reckoned with. He may have presumably possessed all of the standard abilities of a Titan, including immortality, enhanced physical abilities, and great endurance, however as a God of Olympus, he presumably possesses greater abilities. Although while this may indeed be the case, Helios himself does not receive an opportunity to display many of these traits, as his appearances in God of War III were rather brief and did not involve any scuffles with Kratos. However, despite that the God of the Sun is generally described in the lore of the God of War series to be a powerful and essential deity among the Olympians and the wider Greek Pantheon. Notably, the Power of the Sun that he commands due to his mastery of the Primordial Fire grants him the power to destroy the world itself.

Since he is the literal aspect of the Sun, should Helios be destroyed or abducted, this would cause the Sun to be blocked out by heavy rain clouds and violent storms and even disappear entirely (as shown by his death at the hands of Kratos and his abduction in God of War: Chains of Olympus). In addition to all of his primary powers and abilities, Helios also possessed an immense flying chariot with flaming horses that he would ride with very masterful skill into battle at great speeds. He was also in possession of his trademark Sun Shield (worn on his left forearm), which he could use to deflect any oncoming attacks.

Helios was strongly associated with magic and its practice by the mortals. His godly power has been described as all-encompassing in its magical potential.

candidates.title: Exemplar

The Exemplar is a miniboss which can only appear at the Oblivion's Rampart in region 3, just before the inn, starting from Act 3. The Exemplar appears to be two entities, or one creature composed of two, with a headless, humanoid torso emerging from a beast-like mass of grotesque flesh, humanoid arms, and an iron mask similar to the ones worn by Deacon and Cardinal adorning a spot at the end of its spine. The two "halves" of the Exemplar even seem to each be in charge of different skills, with the lower, beast-like half attacking with its huge limbs during "Prelude," and piercing heroes with its gaze during "Rapturous Beauty," while the upper, more humanoid half becomes more animated when destroying an ally with "Pillar of Sacrifice," or when calling forth "The Fall.

The Exemplar functions as a gatekeeper, ensuring that the player is capable of disposing of strong foes before they reach The Mountain. Its attacks are highly damaging, and they can target multiple Heroes, inflict high amounts of , apply debuffs or , and apply to player heroes.

The Exemplar also begins the encounter with an Altar but can kill and resummons different cultist minions. The Exemplar will periodically kill and resummons its allies over the course of the battle, applying self buffs in the process.

candidates.title: Falco
candidates.text:
Falco is a seemingly older man of average height and build. He has semi-long, dark brown hair, slightly parted in the middle, that blooms out to the sides and a thick, but neat mustache that curls up at the ends. He wears Western-style clothes, such as a multi-tone brown waistcoat with suspender-like straps around the shoulders, over a white, high collar shirt with long sleeves. The right sleeve is rolled up to reveal his only obvious cyberware enhancement: a single, silver and black cyberarm of unknown make or model. He wears dark brown pants and light brown shoes. Around his hips hangs a yellow ammo belt with a single, holstered Techtonika Burya on the right side. He has a notable, Southern drawl. The vehicle he drives for Maine's crew is a customized Chevillon Emperor.

Falco serves as a reliable driver throughout the series, never questioning his orders and effectively doing his duties with a high level of composure. He is relatively distant from the crew, sharing no on-screen intimacy with any of them, but cares for them nonetheless, lapsing into moments of outrage when other crew members are harmed. For example, he knocks out Maine after Kiwi is assaulted by him.

His driving skills are put to the test later in the series, after the crew loses Maine and Dorio. His ability to use the Chevillon Emperor as both a vehicle and weapon becomes instrumental to David. He is, most importantly, a man of his word, keeping his promise to David at the end of the show.

candidates.title: The Baron's Call: Free Update for Desperados III with new content released today
candidates.text:
Vienna, Austria/ Munich, Germany, July 23rd, 2020: The critically acclaimed Desperados III isn't challenging enough for you yet? Well, Mimimi Games has got you covered with a free update for all platforms today: introducing the "Baron's Challenge Mission Pack #1", containing four brand new Baron's Challenges for Flagstone, Mayor Higgins' Estate, Eagle Falls, and the Casa DeVitt.

Each one has a new special challenge for you:

- Vanishing Act: A certain snake-oil salesman is peddling his wares at the town square of Flagstone. Make him disappear.
- Untitled Voodoo Mission: Isabelle is about to crash Mayor Higgins' wedding, and she has brought a LOT of mind control darts.
- Public Transportation: Two dead men must be carried to the Eagle Falls train station. The guards won't shoot on sight, but if they see a body...
- Bird Hunting: Doc is perched on the roof of Casa DeVitt, with plenty of ammo and five targets on his list. The party is still going. Happy hunting.

Watch the Trailer: https://youtu.be/nZT3rPHS56Q

Additionally to the new content, Mimimi Games has also improved the game in many ways, for example offering a Borderless Fullscreen Mode or Enhanced Renderscale Support, as well as support of the Tobii Eyetracking Tool.
Find the full patch notes here: http://n.thq.com/PVVx30qZX4M

The official Desperados Pen & Paper RPG is available as a free download.
Watch the trailer: https://youtu.be/xnh82ttKIw0
Download here: https://www.drivethrurpg.com/product/316116/Desperados-A-Pen-and-Paper-Roleplaying-Game

candidates.title: Best Served Cold
candidates.text: Your long awaited visit to New Orleans is interrupted when the Baron arrives with a new challenge for you. He wants you to extract an old associate of his from the busy market and deliver him, dead or alive, to the Baron's private steamboat at Pier 9.

candidates.title: Three Men With No Name
candidates.text: You have taken a trip to Baton Rouge, where another of the Baron's challenges awaits you. He wants you to deliver the bodies of three targets to the coffins inside the bank. However, you don't know where they are, only that they look exactly like a certain someone.

candidates.title: Baron Challenges
candidates.text:
At release (June 16th, 2020), the game only featured five Baron challenges: Contact!, The Devil is in the Details, For a Few Bullets More, Hazards of the Trade, and One Woman Army. However, most of the parts for the other challenges, including their descriptions, was already in the game at that time.
On July 23rd, 2020, the next four challenges were released: Vanishing Act, Untitled Voodoo Mission, Public Transportation, Bird Hunting
On August 20th, 2020, another four challenges were released: Rescue Aid Society, Three Men With No Name, Bear Trap Triplets, Best Served Cold
Finally, on September 2nd, 2020, the last challenge was released together with the first DLC: What If?
In Best Served Cold, The Baron is hinted to be from New Orleans, and that only a few people there know his true name.
The Baron is never met in-game, but he's briefly described in the dossiers of The Devil is in the Details and What If?, as a man with dark skin complexion wearing a fine and expensive suit with deep colors, always smiling with his ivory teeth and having eyes that are "impossibly bright".

candidates.title: Another FREE CONTENT UPDATE introducing 4 new Baron's Challenge missions!
candidates.text:
A Cat, a Chicken, a Dog and a Speedrun Contest: Another Free Update for Desperados III

Vienna, Austria/ Munich, Germany, August 20th, 2020: A cat, a dog and a chicken walk into the town. In the end, Doc McCoy is free! It may sound like the beginning of an epic joke, but is indeed the description of one of the four new Baron's Challenges, added to Desperados III for free. In the Rescue Aid Society Challenge, you take control of Stella the Cat, Agent Floofs, and Sergeant Cluckers! These three unlikely heroes might end McCoy's imprisonment if their skills are used wisely. What do the free challenges have to offer? Take a look:

- Three Men with No Name: Where is Waldo? Identify three specific guards among the crowd of supposed doppelgangers on the map – and kill them!
- Bear Trap Triplets: We all know how much Hector loves his little Bianca. One can only imagine what he could do with three of them... why not put it to a test?
- Best Served Cold: Some poor guy didn't know who the Baron was and cheated him. The Baron wants him found in a crowded market place and brought to the docks – dead or alive.
- Rescue Aid Society: Alas! Doc McCoy is being held prisoner in the Bayous. Isabelle's cat Stella, a dog, and a chicken have formed a special animal commando to rescue the Doc.

Watch the Trailer: https://youtu.be/lPbcNKrK4L8

Find the full patch notes here: http://n.thq.com/k95e30r5jcS
